Also Grégory Glas, Lead Technical Manager signed — that's the signatory; person_responsible is Mannie Panesar (Head of Technical Services). I could include person_responsible: "Mannie Panesar", person_title: "Head of Technical Services". Maybe mention Grégory Glas somewhere? Schema doesn't have signer field. - Xiamen Balance Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., Room 1001-1, No.15-16, Tongan Industrial Park, Meixi Road, Tongan District, Xiamen, PR China

Manufacturers: "The applicant" — so manufacturer is the same as applicant. I'll list with name same as applicant name.

Certified type:
- category: this is a weighing instrument (non-automatic weighing instrument). Category examples given: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system"... The instrument is described as "self-indicating, dual-interval, non-automatic weighing instruments" — the weighing module (A/D board) of a BPS indicator plus main PCB connected to load cells. So category could be "Non-automatic weighing instrument" or "Weighing module". The certified type: "W23 and C Series (C01, C02 and C03 models)". I'll use category "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — hmm, the instrument comprises the weighing module of a BPS indicator and a main PCB connected to load cells to form... weighing instruments. Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument (weighing module)". Keep it simple: "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- type_designations: ["W23", "C01", "C02", "C03"] — also "W23 and C Series". Maybe include "C Series"? type_designations should be all type/model identifiers: W23, C01, C02, C03. The series name "W23 and C Series" — family_name could be "W23 and C Series".
- module_designation: not applicable here (that's for modules like "Analog load cell"). The certificate covers complete instruments (weighing module + main PCB + load cells). I'll set null or omit. Schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. I'll put null or omit. Since not stated, omit... Actually rule 8 says omit if not present. I'll omit module_designation.
- description: "The W23 and C Series comprises the weighing module (A/D board) of a BPS indicator and a main PCB connected to a range of load cells to form a family of Class III, I/O line powered or battery-operated, self-indicating, dual-interval, non-automatic weighing instruments. The instrument is intended to be used for direct sales to the public when connected to a Point of Sale device."

Model family:
- family_name: "W23 and C Series"
- models: W23, C01, C02, C03 with attributes from the model table:
  - W23: display LCD, keyboard None, IOs RS232, options USB, remarks "No keys"
  - C01: LCD, 4 keys, RS232, USB, remarks "4 keys: Light, Function, Zero and Tare." (rowspan spans C01, C02, C03)
  - C02: LCD, 4 keys, RS232, USB, same remark
  - C03: LCD, 4 keys, RS232, USB, same remark

Characteristics type_level (whole-cert attributes from Technical data — the weighing module A/D board):
- power supply: 100 V – 230 Vac, 50/60 Hz; I/O line (USB) 5 VDC; 5 V, 4.0 Ah battery.
  Split:
  - power_supply_voltage: {min: 100, max: 230}, unit V (AC)
  - power_supply_frequency: {min: 50, max: 60}, unit Hz
  - power_supply_type: "AC"
  - Also USB I/O line: 5 VDC — io_line_voltage: 5, unit V
  - battery: 5 V, 4.0 Ah — battery_voltage: 5 V; battery_capacity: 4.0 Ah
- maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: 6000 (they wrote "6 000" — number 6000)
- operating_temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C
- maximum_tare_value: "± ½ Max for single interval" and "± Max1 for dual interval" — these are config-dependent (single vs dual interval). Could be config_level entries: attribute maximum_tare_fraction, axis interval_configuration, values: [{condition: "single interval", value: "0.5 Max"}, {condition: "dual interval", value: "Max1"}]. These are formulas/strings. I'll do config_level with string values "±0.5 × Max" hmm. Value shape requires {value, unit_symbol, unit_id}. In config_level the example: `{condition, value}` — from the schema: "values[]: {condition, value}". And rule 5: "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". So I'll produce entries like {"condition": "single interval", "value": {"value": "±½ Max", ...}} hmm that's nested. Let me re-read.

Schema:
```
config_level[]:                   # attribute × config-axis matrix
    attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}
```

Rule 5: "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}."

So values[] entries: {condition, value, unit_symbol, unit_id?}. The value itself should be number/range/string. For maximum tare: condition "single interval", value "±½ Max" — string (formula). condition "dual interval", value "Max1" or "±Max1". I'll write value strings: "±0.5 Max" hmm. Original: "± ½ Max for single interval", "± Max1 for dual interval". Keep as "±½ Max" and "±Max1". Actually the Max₁ is subscript. I'll write "±Max1".

- load_cell_excitation_voltage: 5, VDC → unit "V DC"? Unit symbol "V". I'll use unit_symbol "V" and value 5. Maybe attribute load_cell_excitation_voltage, value 5, unit_symbol "V". Could note DC in attribute. Keep unit_symbol "V".
- load_cell_impedance: 350, Ω
- minimum_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval: 1.5, μV
- measuring_range_minimum_voltage: 0, mV
- measuring_range_maximum_voltage: 19.5, mV
- fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error: "Pi = 0.5" → attribute fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error (apportionment factor?), value 0.5. Symbol Pi. I'll name it "fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error_pi" with value 0.5. Or apportionment_factor? For R76, Pi = 0.5 is the fraction of mpe for the module. I'll use "fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error" with value 0.5, maybe mention Pi in attribute name: "fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error_pi". Fine.
- load_cell_cable_maximum_length: "0.45 m/mm² (4-wire configuration)" — this is a cross-section dependent length: 0.45 m per mm². Value 0.45, unit "m/mm²". Could be config_level with axis "wiring configuration" (4-wire). I'll do config_level: attribute load_cell_cable_maximum_length, axis "wiring configuration", values: [{condition: "4-wire configuration", value: 0.45, unit_symbol: "m/mm²"}]. Or type_level with footnote in description. Config_level seems apt.

Load cell section (ZEMIC L6D alternative):
- max: 15/30 kg → two values {15, 30} — this is per-model (Max 15 kg or 30 kg). Hmm. "Max (kg): 15/30" — the L6D can be used with Max of 15 or 30 kg. e = 5/10 g correspondingly. Min = 100 g. T = - 14.995 kg (subtractive tare). Load cell Emax = 40 kg.

This is a table of characteristics for fitting the ZEMIC L6D load cell. Max 15/30 and e 5/10 are paired (15→5, 30→10). This is a model/variant matrix of sorts: two configurations. I could capture this as matrix_tables entry "ZEMIC L6D load cell fitting data" with rows for two variants: {max_kg: 15, min_g: 100, e_g: 5, tare_kg: 14.995, load_cell_emax_kg: 40} and {max_kg: 30, min_g: 100, e_g: 10, tare_kg: 14.995, load_cell_emax_kg: 40}.

Or as config_level with axis "capacity configuration". I think matrix_table plus maybe config_level. Let me do matrix_tables entry and also components for the load cell.

Components: The cert names the weighing module (A/D board of BPS indicator) + main PCB, and optionally ZEMIC L6D load cell as alternative to any compatible load cell. Components:
- role: "weighing module (A/D board)" type_designations: [] — no designation given. Hmm. The schema: components[].role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. 
  - component: role "Weighing module (A/D board of BPS indicator)", type_designations: [] (none given).
  - component: role "Main PCB".
  - component: role "Load cell", type_designations: ["ZEMIC L6D"] (specific alternative), alternatives? The rule: "Any compatible load cell OR ZEMIC L6D". I could record alternatives "OR" with type_designations ["any compatible R60 load cell with standard transmission", "ZEMIC L6D"]. Hmm, alternatives field is for when cert offers alternatives among named types. I'll include the load cell component with type_designations ["L6D"] and characteristics: maximum_capacity {min 15, max 30} kg? Actually the two Max values 15/30 pair with e 5/10.

Let me structure the L6D characteristics:
- maximum_capacity: value {min: 15, max: 30}, unit kg — hmm, a range 15–30 isn't accurate; it's two discrete options. But rule 2 says lists of values for Emax → model matrix. Here it's a small table. I could model two variants in the matrix table, which I'll do. In components characteristics, I could put:
  - minimum_capacity: 100 g
  - verification_scale_interval: {min: 5, max: 10} g
  - subtractive_tare_maximum: 14.995 kg
  - load_cell_maximum_capacity: 40 kg

Given the pairing ambiguity, matrix_tables handles it well. I'll add matrix_tables entry:

{
  "name": "ZEMIC L6D load cell fitting data",
  "columns": ["maximum_capacity", "minimum_capacity", "verification_scale_interval", "maximum_subtractive_tare", "load_cell_emax"],
  "column_units": ["kg", "g", "g", "kg", "kg"],
  "rows": [
    {"maximum_capacity": 15, "minimum_capacity": 100, "verification_scale_interval": 5, "maximum_subtractive_tare": 14.995, "load_cell_emax": 40},
    {"maximum_capacity": 30, "minimum_capacity": 100, "verification_scale_interval": 10, "maximum_subtractive_tare": 14.995, "load_cell_emax": 40}
  ]
}

Wait, "T = - (kg): 14.995" — T = - means subtractive tare, T = -14.995 kg? The table row "T = - (kg)" value 14.995. So maximum subtractive tare = 14.995 kg (which is Max 15 minus e 5g? 15 kg - 0.005 kg = 14.995 kg). Yes.

Also config_level could capture single/dual interval tare. Let me do:

config_level:
[
  {
    "attribute": "maximum_tare_value",
    "axis": "interval configuration",
    "values": [
      {"condition": "single interval", "value": "±½ Max", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null},
      {"condition": "dual interval", "value": "±Max1", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}
    ]
  },
  {
    "attribute": "load_cell_cable_maximum_length",
    "axis": "wiring configuration",
    "values": [
      {"condition": "4-wire configuration", "value": 0.45, "unit_symbol": "m/mm²", "unit_id": null}
    ]
  }
]

Also devices: initial zero setting device ≤ 20% of Max; semi-automatic zero setting ≤ 4% of Max for C models; zero tracking optional ≤ 4% Max; tare balancing T = ±Max1.

These could be characteristics with percentage of Max references:
- initial_zero_setting_range: value {min: null, max: 20}, unit "%", plus reference. Value "≤20% of Max". I'll add type_level:
  - initial_zero_setting_range: {value: {min: null, max: 20}, unit_symbol: "%"}
  - semi_automatic_zero_setting_range: {value: {min: null, max: 4}, unit_symbol: "%"} — for C models only. Config? It says "for C models". Could be model_level: attribute semi_automatic_zero_setting_range, values: [{model: "W23", value: "not available"}, {model: "C01", value: 4}, ...]. Hmm. That's model-varying. Rule 4: varying attributes → model_level. I'll do model_level with value 4 for C models and null/absent for W23? Values must have value; for W23 the device isn't present. I could include {"model": "W23", "value": "not fitted"}. Hmm, that introduces strings. Alternatively note in the models' attributes: W23 keyboard "None", C models keyboard "4 keys". And the zero device... The devices list says semi-automatic zero setting device for C models. I'll add model_level entry with values: W23 null? Schema example doesn't show null values but {"model": "W23", "value": null} is acceptable-ish. I think I'll include it: {"model": "W23", "value": null, "footnote_markers": []} — hmm "value": null might be odd. Actually not fabricated: it's a fact that W23 lacks it ("No keys"). I'll include value null for W23 and 4 (%) for C01/C02/C03.

Hmm, but risk of over-engineering. Let me be pragmatic: include model_level for:
- display: LCD (same for all — type_level? It's constant, but it's in the model table; could be in models[].attributes instead). I'll put display, keyboard, IOs, options, remarks into models[].attributes per schema "attributes{}".
- semi_automatic_zero_setting_range: model_level.

Also zero tracking: optional ≤ 4% Max — type_level: zero_tracking_range {max: 4, unit "%"}, optional. Add attribute zero_tracking_range with value {min:null, max:4}, unit "%" and maybe note "optional" — the schema doesn't have an optional flag. I'll skip zero tracking or include with value 4%. I'll include: zero_tracking_range: {value: {min: null, max: 4}, unit_symbol: "%"} — but "optional" info lost. Could add as separate characteristic "zero_tracking": "optional". Eh. I'll include both minimal.

Actually, careful not to bloat. Key numeric data:

Accuracy class III. Dual interval. Class: recommendation accuracy_classes: ["III"].

Recommendation: R76. Canonical id "R76". Edition 2006 (as "OIML R 76-1, Edition: 2006"). The recommendation is R 76-1. id canonical: "R76-1"? The schema example says id e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60". Here it's R 76-1, part 1. I'll use id "R76-1", edition 2006, amendment null, scheme "A", accuracy_classes ["III"].

Hmm.

- W23: "semi_automatic_zero_setting_device": "not fitted" (derived from "None" keyboard? Actually it says "for C models"). The devices section explicitly: "Semi-automatic zero setting device (≤ 4% of Max) for C models". So W23 lacks it.
